finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches any URL whose hostname merely ends with the string 'example.com', so an attacker can register a domain such as 'attackerexample.com' (or 'x.attackerexample.com') and point its DNS at an internal address (e.g. 127.0.0.1, 10.x, 169.254.169.254). The server then issues a GET to that internal address and returns the response length.
finding.source: mirror.py:11 — query parameter `url: str` on GET /mirror, supplied by any HTTP client that can reach the service (no auth in this file).
finding.sink: mirror.py:16 — `await c.get(url)` via httpx.AsyncClient (outbound server-side HTTP request to an attacker-chosen host).

trace.note: url taken from the query string; no normalisation or allow-list beyond line 13
host = urlparse(url).hostname — the hostname the check is applied to

check is `host.endswith("example.com")` — no leading dot, so 'attackerexample.com' passes. The intended ALLOWED_SUFFIX = ".example.com" (line 7) is defined but never used, which indicates the dot-boundary check was intended and omitted.

fresh httpx.AsyncClient with default settings: no custom resolver, no pinning of the resolved IP, so DNS for the attacker's domain is resolved at request time and can return an internal address (DNS rebinding not required).
c.get(url) issues the request. httpx's default follow_redirects=False, so the initial request is the only hop; a 3xx to an internal address is not followed.
response body is read in full (r.text) and only its length is returned, so the attacker gets a limited oracle (body length / success vs. exception) rather than the body.

finding.guards_checked: (1) Scheme: not checked, but httpx only speaks http/https, so non-HTTP schemes fail. (2) Hostname suffix check at line 13: flawed — no dot boundary, so any registrable domain ending in 'example.com' passes. (3) Direct IP literals (e.g. http://127.0.0.1/) are rejected at line 13 because they don't end in 'example.com'; this blocks the trivial case but not domain-based routing to internal IPs. (4) Redirects: not followed (httpx default), which limits redirect-based bypasses. (5) No private/link-local/loopback IP blocking, no DNS resolution check, no port restriction, no response-size limit, no auth on the route. (6) /ping (line 23) uses a hardcoded URL and is not a finding. Possible parser-differential between urlparse (line 12) and httpx's own URL parser (line 16) for userinfo/backslash forms such as 'http://127.0.0.1\@example.com' was considered but not verified — no httpx version is pinned in the repo and I did not execute it, so treat it as an unverified hypothesis rather than a finding.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is mirror.py:13 `host.endswith("example.com")`, which has no dot boundary, so it is not a closing guard. ALLOWED_SUFFIX (mirror.py:7) is never used, and no allow-list, IP/private-range block, or DNS check exists elsewhere in the file.
verdict.reason: The query parameter `url` (mirror.py:11) is unauthenticated, and the hostname check at mirror.py:13 uses `endswith("example.com")` without a leading dot, so an attacker-registered domain like `attackerexample.com` passes and the request is sent at mirror.py:16 to whatever address that domain resolves to, including internal addresses, with the length of the response returned at mirror.py:17.
